posts.author: Ulqiuo
posts.body:
Hi there, just thought I'd pop a post on here to say hi! Been a fan ever since the VX Ace variant of the engine was the one to use, now moving onto MV and starting production on an 8-bit inspired RPG.
Here's hoping for a great start! Nice to meet ya'll!

posts.author: NachoBelle
posts.body: Hi there!! I am also new here but just wanted to offer a welcome! 8-Bit sounds cool! cant wait to see what you come up with! How are you finding MV? im too old to transition to new things and still using VXA haha!

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
@NachoBelle
Too old? Zombie is virtually shaking his decrepit head. You are never too old! I didn't even find my first RPG Maker version (MZ) until I was 52. Although I do get that changing what you are used to and familiar with can be difficult. But it can also be so rewarding.
But no matter which engine you prefer and choose, all that matters is that you enjoy what you do and it works for you.
All Hail the Powerful and Benevolent RPG Maker God!

posts.author: Ulqiuo
posts.body:
NachoBelle said:
Hi there!! I am also new here but just wanted to offer a welcome! 8-Bit sounds cool! cant wait to see what you come up with! How are you finding MV? im too old to transition to new things and still using VXA haha!
Click to expand...
Hey there NachoBelle! A big welcome to you too! Many thanks to you, much appreciated haha! Aye, 8-bit's a bit of a crutch fer me to be fair, leaning into it although the thought of cutscenes terrifies me! Art's never been my strong point but can't let it hold me back forever!
Mv seems very simple actually...I myself started with Vx Ace around ten-fifteen years ago and, even though nothing came of it at the time, the recent transition to MV was almost seamless; everything feels a mite similar, even deja vu-esque, so I'd recommend getting MV in the future when it's on sale, I noticed it was $12 or so on the official site over Christmas!
Also I'm inclined to agree with ZombieKidzRule too - you're never too old! I'm nearing my mid 30's but it's amazing how quickly things pick up when you have an interest haha! Thanks to the internet we have an over-abundance of tutorials too, definitely helps (I still remember the 'fun' of learning way back...)!
...Wow I can waffle haha! But once again, big thanks to you! Although I'm quite noobish, if there's anything I can help with gimme a shout! There're loads of others on here too who can help (and are probably miles better haha)!

Game development of all kinds is always a challenge but overcoming the challenges is a very rewarding feeling. Don't let the cutscenes deter you from your vision, always a good idea to do a competitive analysis and take ideas from other things that already exist out there and turn them into your own.
Happy to hear the transition to MV has been smooth! I was very much thinking to learn MV for the development of the game my team and i are currently working on, but we have settled for VXA at this time since I have many many years of knowledge on it.
